cities.name: Hampi
cities.overview: A village set among the ruins of Vijayanagara, once one of the largest and richest cities in the world. Boulder-strewn hills, banana fields and the Tungabhadra River surround hundreds of temples and royal buildings.

cities.name: Mysuru
cities.overview: The former capital of the Wodeyar kings, Mysuru is known for its palace, its ten-day Dasara festival, silk, sandalwood and Mysore pak.
cities.history: The seat of the Wadiyar dynasty, who ruled the Kingdom of Mysore for centuries, apart from the period of Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan. The city took its modern form under the Wadiyars in the early 20th century.

cities.name: Madikeri
cities.overview: The main town of Kodagu (Coorg), a misty hill region of coffee and pepper estates and the home of the Kodava people.

cities.name: Gokarna
cities.overview: A temple town on the Karnataka coast, sacred to Lord Shiva, with a string of quiet beaches linked by clifftop trails.

cities.name: Badami
cities.overview: A small town between red sandstone cliffs and a lake, once Vatapi, the capital of the early Chalukya kings. Aihole and Pattadakal are close by.

cities.name: Chikkamagaluru
cities.overview: The district where coffee was first grown in India, with the state's highest peaks, shola forests and trekking trails in the Western Ghats.

cities.name: Shravanabelagola
cities.overview: A Jain pilgrimage town between two hills in Hassan district, crowned by a giant statue of Bahubali.

cities.name: Bengaluru
cities.overview: Karnataka's capital and India's technology city, with old gardens and a pleasant climate, and the starting point for weekend trips to the hills.
cities.history: Kempe Gowda founded a mud fort here in 1537. It later passed to Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan and, after 1799, to the British, who built a large cantonment beside the old town.

cities.name: Hassan
cities.overview: A district town that serves as the base for the Hoysala temples of Belur and Halebidu.

cities.name: Mangaluru
cities.overview: A port city between the Arabian Sea and the Western Ghats, the base for the temples and beaches of the Tulu coast.

cities.name: Udupi
cities.overview: A coastal temple town, the home of the Krishna Matha and of the south Indian vegetarian restaurant tradition, with beaches at Malpe.

cities.name: Vijayapura
cities.overview: Old Bijapur, capital of the Adil Shahi sultans, filled with some of the Deccan's grandest Islamic monuments.

cities.name: Bidar
cities.overview: A quiet northern city with a vast Bahmani fort and a well-known tradition of inlaid metalwork.

cities.name: Chitradurga
cities.overview: A town in central Karnataka, under the walls of its stone fort.

cities.name: Shivamogga
cities.overview: The gateway to the Malnad, with Jog Falls and the rainforest of Agumbe within reach.

cities.name: Dandeli
cities.overview: A forest town on the Kali River, a centre for rafting and wildlife in the north of the Western Ghats.

places.name: Group of Monuments at Hampi
places.shortDescription: The vast ruins of the Vijayanagara capital, scattered across a surreal landscape of granite boulders.
places.description: Hampi's ruins cover more than 25 square kilometres. The Virupaksha Temple is still in worship; the Vittala Temple has the famous stone chariot and 'musical' pillars; the Royal Enclosure has the Lotus Mahal, the Elephant Stables and a stepped tank. Explore by bicycle, moped or auto-rickshaw, cross the river by coracle, and climb Matanga Hill or Hemakuta Hill for sunrise or sunset.
places.history: Vijayanagara was the capital of an empire that ruled much of South India from the 14th to the 16th century. It was sacked after the Battle of Talikota in 1565 and abandoned. It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.
places.bestTimeNote: October to February. The Hampi Utsav festival is usually held in winter.

entryFee.note: The ticket covers the Vittala Temple, Lotus Mahal and Elephant Stables on the same day.

highlights: Stone chariot at the Vittala Temple

sources.title: Group of Monuments at Hampi – UNESCO

images.alt: Group of Monuments at Hampi, Hampi

places.name: Mysuru Palace
places.shortDescription: The ornate palace of the Wodeyar kings, lit up by nearly 100,000 bulbs on Sunday evenings and during Dasara.
places.description: Mysuru Palace mixes Hindu, Mughal, Rajput and Gothic styles beneath its grey granite domes. Inside are the stained-glass Kalyana Mantapa (marriage hall), the pillared Durbar Hall, and galleries of paintings and royal artefacts. Shoes must be left outside and photography is restricted indoors. Come back after dark on a Sunday or public holiday to see the whole palace lit.
places.history: The present palace was designed by the British architect Henry Irwin and completed in 1912, after the earlier wooden palace burned down in 1897. It is the centre of the Mysuru Dasara festival, which the Wodeyars have celebrated since the 17th century.
places.bestTimeNote: October for Dasara (dates vary each year); otherwise October to February.

entryFee.note: Ticketed; foreigners pay more. Check the official palace site for current rates.

timings.hours: 10:00 AM – 5:30 PM; illumination on Sundays and holidays 7:00–7:45 PM

location.address: Sayyaji Rao Road, Agrahara, Chamrajpura, Mysuru, Karnataka 570001

places.name: Abbey Falls
places.shortDescription: A waterfall tucked between coffee and spice plantations, a short walk from Madikeri.
places.description: A paved path leads down through coffee bushes, pepper vines and cardamom to a hanging bridge facing Abbey (Abbi) Falls, which tumble about 20 metres over rocks. It is at its most powerful during and just after the monsoon. Combine it with Raja's Seat for sunset and a coffee-estate stay.
places.bestTimeNote: July to December; the flow is weak in summer.

location.address: Abbey Falls Road, Madikeri, Kodagu district, Karnataka 571201

places.name: Om Beach
places.shortDescription: A beach shaped like the Om symbol, on a clifftop trail linking Gokarna's quiet coves.
places.description: Om Beach is the best known of the beaches south of Gokarna town, with two curved bays joined by a rocky point. Many visitors walk the coastal trail from Kudle Beach over Om Beach to Half Moon and Paradise beaches, returning by boat. Water sports and simple shacks operate in season. Currents can be strong; swim only where it's safe.

location.address: Om Beach, Gokarna, Uttara Kannada district, Karnataka 581326

highlights: Beach trek to Half Moon and Paradise

places.name: Badami Cave Temples
places.shortDescription: Four 6th-century rock-cut temples carved into red sandstone cliffs above Agastya Lake.
places.description: Badami's four caves climb the cliff one above another: three are Hindu (dedicated to Shiva and Vishnu) and one is Jain. Look for the 18-armed dancing Shiva in Cave 1 and the large Vishnu reliefs in Cave 3. Across Agastya Lake are the Bhutanatha temples and the North Fort. Nearby Aihole and the UNESCO-listed temples of Pattadakal make an excellent day circuit with far fewer crowds than Hampi.
places.history: Carved under the early Chalukya kings, who made Badami (then Vatapi) their capital in the 6th century. Cave 3 has an inscription dated 578 CE.

entryFee.note: Verify current rates with the Archaeological Survey of India.

highlights: Day trip to Aihole and Pattadakal

places.name: Kudremukh Peak
places.shortDescription: A full-day trek through shola forest and grassland to a 1,894-metre peak shaped like a horse's face.
places.description: The trek to Kudremukh is about 20 km round trip, crossing streams and rolling green grassland inside Kudremukh National Park. On clear days the summit looks out over the Western Ghats towards the Arabian Sea. A forest-department permit and a guide are required, and the number of trekkers per day is limited, so book ahead.
places.bestTimeNote: October to February. Treks are usually closed during the monsoon.

entryFee.note: Trek permit and guide fees; book through the Karnataka forest department.

timings.hours: Treks start early in the morning

location.address: Kudremukh National Park, Chikkamagaluru district, Karnataka 577142

highlights: Summit views of the Western Ghats

places.name: Gommateshwara, Shravanabelagola
places.shortDescription: A 17-metre monolithic statue of Bahubali on a granite hill, one of the largest free-standing statues in the world.
places.description: About 600 rock-cut steps climb Vindhyagiri hill to the serene, unclothed figure of Bahubali (Gommateshwara), carved from a single block of granite, with vines climbing his legs to show his long meditation. The opposite hill, Chandragiri, has old Jain temples and inscriptions. Climb barefoot early in the morning before the rock heats up.
places.history: The statue was commissioned around 981 CE by Chavundaraya, a minister of the Western Ganga dynasty. Every twelve years the Mahamastakabhisheka festival bathes it in milk, saffron and flowers; the last was held in 2018.

location.address: Vindhyagiri Hill, Shravanabelagola, Hassan district, Karnataka 573135

places.name: Lalbagh Botanical Garden
places.shortDescription: A 240-acre botanical garden from 1760 in the middle of Bengaluru, with a Victorian glasshouse.
places.description: Old trees, lawns and a glasshouse modelled on London's Crystal Palace. The garden comes alive with flower shows around Republic Day and Independence Day.
places.history: Originally built by Hyder Ali in 1760 and developed by his son Tipu Sultan and by a series of British superintendents.

places.name: Cubbon Park
places.shortDescription: The green lung in Bengaluru's business district, laid out in 1870 and full of bamboo and old rain trees.
places.description: Morning walkers and runners fill the paths through a large park in the heart of the city. The High Court and the State Library sit among the trees.
places.history: Created in 1870 under Major General Richard Sankey, and now officially Sri Chamarajendra Park.

places.name: Bengaluru Palace
places.shortDescription: An 1874 Tudor-style palace of the Mysore Maharajas, in the north of the city.
places.description: Turrets and battlements inspired by Windsor Castle, with wood-carved interiors and a small collection of old royal photos. The grounds host big concerts.
places.history: Commissioned by the Maharaja of Mysore and completed in 1874.

places.name: Bannerghatta National Park
places.shortDescription: A national park with a zoo and safari at the edge of Bengaluru.
places.description: Forest and scrub on the southern edge of the city, with bus safaris past lions, tigers and bears. India's first butterfly park is also here.
places.history: Founded in 1970, declared a national park in 1974. A small part of it became a zoo in 2002.

places.name: Tipu Sultan's Summer Palace
places.shortDescription: A two-storey teak palace in the old city, an elegant survival of Tipu Sultan's Bengaluru.
places.description: A wooden palace with painted arches and balconies, built inside the walls of the old Bangalore Fort. There's a small museum on Tipu and his father.
places.history: Hyder Ali began the building, and Tipu Sultan finished it.
highlights: Near KR Market and old fort

places.name: Nandi Hills
places.shortDescription: An old hill fortress about 60 km from Bengaluru, loved for its sunrise above the clouds.
places.description: Bengaluru's classic early-morning drive: you arrive before dawn to watch the sun come up over a valley of mist, then walk through the old fort and temples.
places.history: An ancient hill fortress built by the Ganga dynasty and later strengthened by Tipu Sultan.
highlights: Bhoga Nandeeshwara Temple at the foot

places.name: Chamundi Hills
places.shortDescription: The hill above Mysuru, topped by the Chamundeshwari Temple and a giant monolithic Nandi.
places.description: A 1,000-step walk or a short drive brings you to the temple of the city's patron goddess, passing a huge black stone Nandi on the way. The view takes in the palace and the city.

places.name: Brindavan Gardens
places.shortDescription: Terraced gardens below the Krishnarajasagara Dam on the Kaveri, with an evening musical fountain.
places.description: Formal terraced gardens lie at the foot of the great dam, 12 km from the city. The evening musical fountain is the reason most people come.
places.history: Laid out alongside the Krishnarajasagara Dam in the time of the Wadiyars.

places.name: St. Philomena's Cathedral
places.shortDescription: A Neo-Gothic cathedral with twin spires that rise over the Mysuru skyline.
places.description: A tall Gothic cathedral modelled on Cologne's, with stained glass showing scenes from the life of Christ and a crypt below.
highlights: Crypt with a relic of St. Philomena

places.name: Mysuru Zoo
places.shortDescription: One of India's oldest and best-loved zoos, right in the city, with 157 acres of gardens.
places.description: A well-kept zoo next to the palace, with gorillas, giraffes, elephants and big cats. Plan a good half day here.
places.history: Founded under royal patronage in the 19th century as Sri Chamarajendra Zoological Gardens.

places.name: Srirangapatna
places.shortDescription: An island town on the Kaveri, once Tipu Sultan's capital, 15 km from Mysuru.
places.description: Temples, a palace, tombs and fort walls packed onto a river island. Tipu's Daria Daulat palace has painted walls, and his tomb, the Gumbaz, stands in a quiet garden.
places.history: The capital of Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan; Tipu died here in 1799 when the British stormed the fort. It takes its name from the Ranganathaswamy Temple, consecrated around 984 CE.

places.name: Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary
places.shortDescription: Karnataka's largest bird sanctuary, six islets on the Kaveri where boats drift past nesting storks and crocodiles.
places.description: A short boat trip brings you close to painted storks, spoonbills and egrets, with crocodiles basking on the rocks. Small in area and big on birds.

places.name: Somanathapura Temple
places.shortDescription: A small and perfect Hoysala star-shaped temple from 1258 on the bank of the Kaveri.
places.description: Three carved towers rise on a star-shaped platform. It's the most complete Hoysala temple, and it's rarely crowded. The panels of gods and epic scenes are remarkably fine.
places.history: Consecrated in 1258 CE by Somanatha, a general of the Hoysala king Narasimha III.

places.name: Shivanasamudra Falls
places.shortDescription: A pair of wide waterfalls on the Kaveri, Gagana Chukki and Bhara Chukki, between Bengaluru and Mysuru.
places.description: The Kaveri splits around an island and plunges in two broad curtains, loudest right after the monsoon. One of Asia's earliest hydroelectric stations was built here in 1902.

places.name: Bandipur National Park
places.shortDescription: A dry forest tiger reserve between Mysuru and Ooty, part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve.
places.description: Elephant herds, gaur and spotted deer are common, and tigers do appear. The park merges with Mudumalai and Wayanad across state lines.
places.history: Established as a tiger reserve under Project Tiger in 1973.

places.name: Nagarhole National Park
places.shortDescription: A rich forest in Kodagu and Mysuru districts, known for elephants and the Kabini backwaters.
places.description: Teak and rosewood forest runs down to the Kabini River, where herds of elephants gather in summer. It's among the best places in India to see leopards and wild dogs.
places.history: Declared the 37th tiger reserve of India in 2003.

places.name: Chennakeshava Temple, Belur
places.shortDescription: A 12th-century Hoysala masterpiece, still in worship, with hundreds of carved figures. UNESCO-listed.
places.description: Star-shaped and low, covered with bracket figures of dancers and a wall of friezes showing elephants, lions and epics. Not one pillar in the Navaranga hall matches another.
places.history: Commissioned by King Vishnuvardhana in 1117 CE. Part of the Hoysala temples on the UNESCO list.

places.name: Hoysaleswara Temple, Halebidu
places.shortDescription: The Shiva temple at the old Hoysala capital, with some of the finest stone friezes in India.
places.description: Twin shrines on a star base, with miles of frieze showing elephants, lions, horses and Hindu epics. Two huge Nandi bulls sit outside.
places.history: A 12th-century temple in Halebidu, the former Hoysala capital, which was sacked in the 14th century.

places.name: Talakaveri
places.shortDescription: The source of the River Kaveri, a holy tank high in the Brahmagiri hills of Kodagu.
places.description: A small tank near the top of the Brahmagiri hills marks where the Kaveri begins. Steps climb behind it for a view over the Western Ghats.

places.name: Namdroling Monastery
places.shortDescription: The Golden Temple of Bylakuppe, the largest teaching centre of the Nyingma school of Tibetan Buddhism.
places.description: Painted halls with giant golden Buddhas stand at the heart of a Tibetan settlement in the Karnataka countryside. It feels a long way from the rest of south India.

places.name: Mahabaleshwar Temple, Gokarna
places.shortDescription: A 4th-century Shiva temple on the Gokarna shore, known for the Atmalinga in its sanctum.
places.description: An old Dravidian-style temple on the seafront, and the focus of the town's pilgrim life. Non-Hindus may not always be allowed inside the sanctum.

places.name: Murudeshwara
places.shortDescription: A seaside Shiva temple with the world's third tallest Shiva statue, on a headland in the Arabian Sea.
places.description: A giant statue of Shiva and a towering temple gopuram stand on a small peninsula, surrounded by the sea. The town also has a beach and scuba trips to Netrani Island.
highlights: Lift to the top of the gopuram

places.name: Udupi Sri Krishna Matha
places.shortDescription: A historic Krishna temple and Dvaita monastery at the heart of Udupi.
places.description: A busy temple in which the deity is viewed through a small carved window, the Kanakana Kindi. Thousands are fed here each day, and the eight monasteries around it take turns running it.
places.history: Founded by the philosopher Madhvacharya in the 13th century.
highlights: Rath chariots in the car street

places.name: St. Mary's Islands
places.shortDescription: Four small islands off Malpe, known for their hexagonal columns of basalt.
places.description: A short boat ride from Malpe Beach brings you to tiny islands of coconut palms and shells, with honeycomb-shaped basalt columns along the shore.
places.bestTimeNote: Boats generally don't run during the monsoon, from June to September.

places.name: Kollur Mookambika Temple
places.shortDescription: A revered temple of the goddess Mookambika, in the forested foothills of Kodachadri.
places.description: A major pilgrimage centre under the Western Ghats, with many visitors from Kerala. The Kodachadri peak nearby makes a popular trek.

places.name: Panambur Beach
places.shortDescription: Mangaluru's most popular beach, with lifeguards and water sports, 10 km north of the city.
places.description: A wide stretch of sand beside the New Mangalore Port, with jet skis and kite festivals. Well-looked-after by local standards.

places.name: Dharmasthala Temple
places.shortDescription: An 800-year-old temple town in Dakshina Kannada, with a Shiva shrine run by a Jain family.
places.description: A remarkable institution in which Hindu priests serve a Shiva temple managed by a Jain family. Huge kitchens feed thousands each day, and a giant statue of Bahubali stands nearby.

places.name: Mullayanagiri
places.shortDescription: The highest peak in Karnataka at 1,925 m, an easy climb among coffee estates and shola forest.
places.description: A road goes nearly to the top, and a stone stairway completes the climb to a small temple. Cloud rolls over the ridge and over the slopes of Baba Budan Giri.
highlights: Trail across to Baba Budan Giri

places.name: Sringeri
places.shortDescription: A hill town on the Tunga River, seat of the first monastery of Adi Shankara.
places.description: The Sri Sharadamba temple and the 14th-century Vidyashankara Temple stand on the river bank in the green Malnad hills, where the fish are fed by pilgrims.
places.history: The site of the Sringeri Sharada Peetham, established by Adi Shankara.

places.name: Jog Falls
places.shortDescription: A 253 m plunge of the Sharavati River in four cascades, one of India's highest waterfalls.
places.description: Raja, Rani, Rover and Rocket fall side by side into a deep gorge. Worth seeing during and right after the monsoon, when they are full.
places.bestTimeNote: Flow is regulated by the Linganamakki Dam upstream, and the falls can be thin in summer.
highlights: Raja, Rani, Rover and Rocket falls

places.name: Agumbe
places.shortDescription: A rainforest village in the Western Ghats, known for heavy rain, king cobras and sunset views.
places.description: One of the wettest places in south India, with old tiled houses, ghat road bends and a sunset viewpoint out toward the Arabian Sea. It's also home to a research station for king cobras.

places.name: Dandeli Wildlife Sanctuary
places.shortDescription: A forest reserve in Uttara Kannada, known for hornbills, black panthers and Kali River rafting.
places.description: Tall forest beside the Kali River, known for Malabar pied hornbills and rare black panthers. Dandeli town next door is Karnataka's main white-water rafting base.

places.name: Pattadakal
places.shortDescription: A UNESCO group of 7th and 8th century Chalukya temples on the Malaprabha River, where kings were crowned.
places.description: Temples in northern and southern styles stand next to each other, an experiment in form that you can walk through in an hour. The Virupaksha Temple has the finest carving.
places.history: A complex of Hindu and Jain temples, later used by the Chalukyas for royal coronations.
highlights: Mix of Nagara and Dravida styles

places.name: Aihole
places.shortDescription: A village of more than a hundred Chalukya temples, and the place where Indian temple design was worked out.
places.description: Often called the cradle of Indian temple architecture, with temples from the 6th century scattered among the houses. The apse-shaped Durga Temple is the best known.
places.history: Buddhist, Hindu and Jain monuments here date from the 6th to the 12th century CE.

places.name: Gol Gumbaz
places.shortDescription: A vast 17th-century domed tomb in Vijayapura, famous for its whispering gallery.
places.description: One of the largest domes in the world crowns this grey basalt mausoleum. A whisper in the gallery can be heard clearly across the dome, and it echoes many times over.
places.history: The tomb of Mohammad Adil Shah, seventh ruler of the Bijapur Sultanate.
highlights: One of the world's largest domes

places.name: Ibrahim Rauza
places.shortDescription: An elegant tomb and mosque in Vijayapura, said to have inspired the Taj Mahal.
places.description: A mosque and mausoleum face each other across a pool, in a walled garden. Slender minarets and stone lattice make it far more refined than its big neighbour.
places.history: Built by Ibrahim Adil Shah II, ruler of the Bijapur Sultanate, for himself.

places.name: Bidar Fort
places.shortDescription: A huge Bahmani fort with triple moats and Persian-style palaces in northern Karnataka.
places.description: Seven gates, a triple moat and the ruined palaces of the Bahmani sultans spread across a plateau. The tiled Rangin Mahal is the highlight.
places.history: Sultan Ahmad Shah I of the Bahmani dynasty moved his capital from Gulbarga to Bidar in the 15th century.

places.name: Chitradurga Fort
places.shortDescription: A fort of seven circular walls straddling granite hills in central Karnataka.
places.description: Massive stone ramparts wind around boulder hills, with temples, granaries and water tanks hidden inside. Stories of Onake Obavva, who fought off invaders with a pestle, are told here.
places.history: The British called it Chitaldoorg. It reached its final form under the Nayakas and Tipu Sultan.
